purpose: Measure bounded synthetic execution and crash recovery; no live-model quality inference
hypothesis: One injected worker loss increases attempts and recovery latency while preserving terminal-job, tenant, deduplication and budget invariants
experimental_unit: A fresh database-schema batch of 12 jobs; jobs within a batch share workers and are dependent
ordering: Shuffle the same workload by each seed in both arms; alternate which arm runs first by seed index
fault: SIGKILL exactly one worker after the effect sink records its first invocation; do not artificially expire the lease
approval_actor: Automated deterministic test driver, explicitly not an independent human reviewer
secondary_outcomes: child CPU time and per-process peak RSS
success_criteria: All 72 planned jobs are accounted for; each completed batch has 9 succeeded, 2 intentionally failed and 1 cancelled; each effect has one committed effect; rejected tenant reads disclose no data; persisted budget equals operation accounting; all injected losses are retained
sample_size_rationale: Three matched batches expose deterministic races/recovery repeatedly within a small resource budget; insufficient for production availability or broad performance claims
analysis: Retain failures, timeouts and unstarted work in denominators; report batches separately; pair arms by seed; exploratory seeded batch bootstrap for mean differences with explicit n=3 limitation
limits: Requires dedicated PostgreSQL and Linux processes. Run inside checks container limits: 2 CPUs, 768 MiB, 64 PIDs. No network provider calls, money, public deployment or independent label attestations. Existing exposed tasks stay development-only.
